screening.main_topic: Opposition to the Dakota Access Pipeline, including Indigenous rights, environmental risks, fossil-fuel infrastructure, and related protests and political debate
screening.climate_relevance: The text repeatedly connects the pipeline to fossil-fuel expansion, carbon emissions, climate change, and the transition away from oil. It also includes discussion of climate science, climate policy, and labor organizations’ positions on fossil-fuel infrastructure.
screening.reason: Although much of the text focuses on Indigenous sovereignty, water protection, policing, and protest, climate-related arguments are recurring and substantive: speakers link the pipeline to climate impacts and emissions, call for an end to fossil-fuel infrastructure, and debate climate policy and the energy transition. This makes the material relevant as core climate discourse.
